newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast prods ease as players avoid sales.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast prods ease as players avoid sales.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot product prices were generally lower in spotty Tuesday activity, as wide swings in the NYMEX markets scared buyers out of the market, traders said.
West Coast traders also avoided buying until the American Petroleum Institute (API) released its weekly inventory data Wednesday, a day after its normal reporting time.
"Tomorrow afternoon you may see more activity," said a West Coast broker.
After trading up to 60.20 cents a gallon, NYMEX heating oil for March slid to 59.42 cents, off 1.39 cents from Friday.
And front-month ended 0.09 cents a gallon lower after gaining 0.35 cents early.
Few deals were done on West Coast spot market, with a cargo heard sold at 73 cents a gallon for March barrels of Los Angeles CARB-grade unleaded.
A cargo of CARB diesel sold in L.A. for 80 cents in the freeze, traders said.
Bids for CARB-grade gasoline were talked around a penny off yesterday at 73 cents, while offers were heard about 75 cents, up a penny. Bay area material was about four cents lower.
Conventinal L.A. gasoline ranged about 70 to 70.50, flat with Thursday, with premium still carrying at seven-cent advantage.
Distillates in both cities were unchanged, with CARB diesel in L.A. notionally around 79 to 80 cents a gallon.
